newsitem.title: UK: Brazil rumoured close to rating upgrade, Bradys up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rumoured close to rating upgrade, Bradys up.

text.p: Market talk that Brazil was about to receive an upgrade from at least one of the major rating agencies drove its Brady bond prices higher on Wednesday, dealers said.

"There's a rumour it will be upgraded -- we've been waiting for its Eurobond and one of the reasons for the delay may be that it's haggling for a rating from S&Ps or Moody's," said Stuart Parkinson, fixed income analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
A Brady bond trader at a U.S. bank here said he also thought Brazil was going for a rating upgrade.
"It's possible it may coincide with their global," he added.
Brazil's long term foreign currency debt rating is B-plus with a positive outlook from Standard & Poor's and B1 from Moody's Investors Service.

Traders have been expecting Brazil to launch a Eurobond or a global bond for the last two weeks. Talk of a $750 million issue has now expanded to a $1.0 billion five-year deal. Chase will lead manage the issue.
While no date has been published for the deal's launch, one trader said he had heard it was due next Wednesday.
The market talk drove Brazilian Brady bonds higher on Wednesday, with Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR climbing 1/2 point to 73-3/4.
Moody's and S&P's both declined to comment on the market talk.
